conventions.convention: N ≥ 1, U = {1,…,N}, and all population values are fixed real numbers. Design probability randomizes only the selected subset.
The design support is a nonempty finite family of subsets with strictly positive weights summing to one; zero-weight subsets are omitted. Empty selected subsets are permitted.
Second-order inclusion probabilities include diagonal pairs, with π_ii = π_i.

The common observation space consists of records (s,z), with z a real-valued function on the selected labels s; its sigma-algebra is the full power set. The parameter space is all real population value functions.
Horvitz–Thompson unbiasedness requires every first-order inclusion probability to be positive; the mean estimator divides the estimated total by population size N.
The SRSWOR example assumes N ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ n ≤ N; its pairwise covariance formula concerns distinct units and includes both n = 1 and the census n = N.

load_bearing.statement: A finite population has fixed real values on U = {1,…,N}, N ≥ 1. A sampling design has nonempty finite subset support and strictly positive normalized weights. It defines inclusion probabilities, design expectation, common observed records, and the induced experiment indexed by all population value functions.
For every fixed y ∈ ℝ^U, the set function P_y^d defined in def-finite-population-and-sampling-design is a probability measure on (X_d,A_d).

For a finite population and sampling design with π_i > 0 for every unit, the observed-record maps Σ_{i∈s} z_i/π_i and N⁻¹Σ_{i∈s} z_i/π_i are estimators of the total and mean, respectively, and their expectations under P_y^d equal T(y) and the population mean.
If some unit has π_i = 0, the total estimand in the induced experiment is not identifiable, and no estimator that is a function only of the observed record can be design-unbiased for every y ∈ ℝ^U.

Typing the common observed-record measurable space.
The empty-set and countable-additivity requirements in the induced-law lemma.
Concluding that the normalized induced observed-record measure is a probability measure.
Interpreting normalized design weights and probabilities of sample events.
Finite weighted design expectations, integrability, and equality of expectations for identical records.
Constructing the experiment on one common record space indexed by population value functions.
Treating population total and mean as functions on the parameter space.
Checking that identical observed laws with unequal totals disprove identifiability.
Measurability and target-space requirements for observed-record estimators.
Unbiasedness requires integrability and the correct expectation under every parameter law.
Specifying the real estimator target sigma-algebra.
Identifying unit-inclusion variables as event indicators.
The centered-product covariance definition in the SRSWOR example.
Taking expectations of finite indicator-weighted sums without independence.
Indicator expectations equal inclusion probabilities, and indicator products represent joint inclusion.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and contract Definition against the finite-population Definition. The requirement to record target population and sampling units is faithful; fixed values and the selection law are kept distinct, without an adequacy claim.

Checked both page descriptions and the fixed-design model Definition. Holding X fixed supplies no selection law for X and does not specify a finite-population sampling design, exactly as the batch-8 contrast states.

Checked the downstream definitions and variance theorem uses against the supplier. Fixed values, finite design support, inclusion indicators, and diagonal inclusion probabilities are preserved. Fixed sample size, uniformity, first-order positivity, and pair positivity are imposed locally where needed.

The stratified Definition supplies its own normalized product design. The unbiasedness theorem establishes π_i = n_h/N_h > 0 and identifies the stratified total with the observed-record Horvitz–Thompson estimator before invoking batch 8.

Checked the one-stage and two-stage Definitions against batch 8. They retain fixed values and positive normalized finite design supports. The two-stage joint product law and conditional independence are explicitly additional assumptions; expansion denominators require first-order positivity.

The planning page uses finite-population sampling as design context and expressly does not infer Gaussian errors or exact normal inference from it. Its planning specification ties each candidate to its own declared experiment and sampling law.
